text: Ships a CLI installable globally via npm, usable from any directory
quote: npm i -g foreloop   # installs globally, so the CLI works in any directory

text: foreloop init installs a task-executor skill into a repo checkout so an agent can pick up project tasks there
quote: foreloop init installs the task-executor skill into the checkout, which is what lets an agent working in that directory pick up the project's tasks.

text: An agent (Claude Code or Codex) runs locally in a repo checkout, claims an approved task, and opens a PR from the user's own GitHub account
quote: You run an agent — Claude Code or Codex — in a checkout of your repository on your own machine. That agent asks Foreloop for approved tasks in that repository, claims one, does the work, and opens a pull request from your GitHub account.

text: Users can describe a problem in plain language (e.g. an unclear bug) without knowing which files are affected, and that's enough to start a task
quote: "Users can't tell which invoices are overdue" is enough to start; you do not need to know which files change.

text: Exposes an official MCP server endpoint over streamable HTTP, reachable with just a URL and API key
quote: Foreloop speaks MCP at /api/app/public/v1/mcp over streamable HTTP. An MCP client needs that URL and an API key and nothing else

text: Provides a JS SDK call (initForeloopFeedback) to initialize feedback capture with an API key
Requires explicit human approval of a task contract before an agent can make any repository changes
quote: Nothing runs until a person approves a contract. Approval is the only gate, and the gate is deliberate: an agent is about to change your repository.

text: A Development/Agents view lists each running agent, its assigned checkout name, current task, and last status message
quote: Development, under Agents, lists one row per worker: which agent it is running as, the name that checkout gave itself, the task it holds, and the last thing it said.

text: CLI supports a --json flag on every command with a stable, additive-only output shape suitable for scripting
quote: `--json` works on any command and has a stable shape. Additive changes only.

text: Users can author reusable 'skills' to encode recurring corrections/instructions for agents
quote: Write a skill when you notice yourself giving an agent the same correction twice.

text: Generates shareable links that can be pasted into commit messages or a browser address bar to open a resource directly
quote: Paste one into a commit message or type one into the address bar after the site name to open it directly.

text: An 'intention' is generated from a user-submitted report, with an agent reading the submission and proposing scoped tasks
quote: An intention starts from the report, and its agent reads the submission, fills in the intention, and proposes the tasks

text: Embeddable feedback widget can be added to any web project (Webflow, Framer, WordPress, hand-written HTML) via a single tag, no build step
quote: One tag, and we serve the widget. Right for most web projects — Webflow, Framer, WordPress, or any hand-written HTML. Nothing to build

text: Connecting a GitHub repo lets Foreloop read the codebase and lets an agent open pull requests against it
quote: Connecting GitHub is how Foreloop reads your code, and how an agent opens a pull request against it.

text: CLI can manage projects, loops, intentions, stories, and tasks headlessly from any process that can run a command, including agents and cron jobs
quote: Projects, loops, intentions, stories and tasks from a terminal — and from anything that can run one, including coding agents and cron.

text: Key decisions requiring human judgment can be approved remotely from a phone via an approvals list
quote: Approve the big calls from your phone.

text: Feedback widget lets a user point at a page element and attach the page, metadata, and an optional marked-up screenshot so the agent fixes the correct spot
quote: Pressing the control opens a box where a user can write what went wrong, mark up a screenshot of the screen they are looking at, and send.

text: Feedback widget can use a restricted API key that only carries a signal:write scope, safe to embed in client-side/browser code
quote: A widget key carries only the signal:write scope — it can submit feedback and nothing else, which is why it may live in browser code and in your repository.
